name: San Francisco
intro: This page covers the city itself; the rest of the Bay Area's starred restaurants, from Oakland and Silicon Valley to Napa and Sonoma, are on the California page.

localNote.q: How do you book a Michelin star restaurant in SF?
localNote.a: Online, on whichever app the restaurant uses. OpenTable is the most common, used by {r:saison}, {r:sons-daughters} and others; {r:benu} is on Tock, {r:7-adams} on Resy and {r:quince} on SevenRooms. Most hold a credit card against a late cancellation.

localNote.q: When do tables open at SF’s starred restaurants?
localNote.a: Mostly on the 1st of the month before. Quince and Saison release the following month’s tables then, {r:kiln} at noon Pacific time and Sons & Daughters at midnight. Others roll day by day: 7 Adams 28 days ahead at midnight, {r:mister-jius} 30 days ahead at 10am.

localNote.q: What should you wear to a Michelin star restaurant in SF?
localNote.a: Mostly what you like. Quince asks for cocktail attire and {r:acquerello} suggests jackets for men, but neither requires one, and Sons & Daughters says jeans are welcome.

localNote.q: How much should you tip in SF?
localNote.a: Usually nothing extra. Most of SF’s starred restaurants add a service charge of about 20% in place of a tip (22% at Quince), and some add a few per cent more for staff health care, which the city requires employers to fund. Sons & Daughters, for one, says no further gratuity is expected.
